2) Test run outcome (project-wide) - Command executed earlier: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Jest output: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 266 passed, 266 total - Includes: - "Maintenance CLI (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)" (tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts) - "detectStaleAnnotations (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)" (tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts) - "detectStaleAnnotations isolated (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)" (tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts) - "updateAnnotationReferences (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)" and "isolated" variants - "batchUpdateAnnotations" and "verifyAnnotations" (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS) - "generateMaintenanceReport (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)" - "Maintenance Tools Index Exports (Story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS)"
3) Implementation per requirement - REQ-MAINT-DETECT (Detect stale annotation references) - src/maintenance/detect.ts - export function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Resolves workspaceRoot from process.cwd() and codebasePath; returns [] if root does not exist or is not a directory. - Recursively enumerates files via getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) and scans contents for @story using regex /@story\s+([^\s]+)/g. - Uses isUnsafeStoryPath and enforceProjectBoundary (from ../utils/storyReferenceUtils) to skip unsafe or out-of-project paths. - For in-project candidates, checks existence with fs.existsSync and adds storyPath to a Set when none of the candidates exist. - JSDoc and inline comments reference @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT / REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should return empty array when no stale annotations" (empty temp dir -> []). - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] should detect stale annotation references" (file with @story stale.story.md -> result includes that path). - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - Non-existent directory -> returns []. - Nested directories with multiple stale stories -> both detected. - Permission denied scenario -> expect detectStaleAnnotations(tmpDir2) to throw (low-level error surfaced for direct API call). - Security validation test verifying that malicious/traversal/invalid-extension paths are never passed to existsSync, while normalized inside-workspace and legitimate.story.md paths are checked. - CLI tests: - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts: "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits with code 0 and message when no stale annotations" and JSON output and non-existent --root behavior, exercising handleDetect + CLI wiring.
- REQ-MAINT-UPDATE (Update annotation references) - src/maintenance/update.ts - export function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number - Returns 0 immediately if codebasePath does not exist or is not a directory. - Escapes oldPath for regex, builds RegExp `(@story\s*)${escapedOldPath}` and applies replacement in processFileForAnnotationUpdates. - processFileForAnnotationUpdates: - Skips non-files based on fs.statSync(fullPath).isFile(). - Reads file, performs replacement; increments replacementCountRef.count per match. - Writes file only when content changed. - All key functions are annotated with @story 009.0 and @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] updates @story annotations in files" – writes file with @story old.path.md, runs updateAnnotationReferences, expects count === 1 and content containing @story new.path.md. - Directory-not-exist case returns 0. - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] should return 0 when no updates made" – temp dir with no matching annotations returns 0. - CLI tests (tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts): - "[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update performs replacements and exits 0" – uses runMaintenanceCli with update, asserts exit code 0 and file content updated. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run does not modify files and exits 0" – confirms content unchanged and clear dry-run logs.
- REQ-MAINT-BATCH (Batch updates) - src/maintenance/batch.ts - export function batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings): number - Loops over mappings { oldPath, newPath }, calls updateAnnotationReferences for each, returns summed count. - Annotated with @req REQ-MAINT-BATCH and REQ-MAINT-VERIFY. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-BATCH] should return 0 when no mappings applied" – batchUpdateAnnotations(temp.dir, []) => 0.
- REQ-MAINT-VERIFY (Verify references after maintenance) - src/maintenance/batch.ts - export function verifyAnnotations(codebasePath): boolean - Calls detectStaleAnnotations and returns staleAnnotations.length === 0. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts – creates a temp dir with @story my-story.story.md and actual story file; verifyAnnotations(temp.dir) returns true. - CLI: tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts – "[REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits with code 0 when annotations valid", ensuring exit code and log behavior for handleVerify.
- REQ-MAINT-REPORT (Generate reports) - src/maintenance/report.ts - export function generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string - Uses detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath). - Returns "" when no stale annotations; otherwise returns staleAnnotations.join("\n"). - Comments explicitly tie behavior to REQ-MAINT-REPORT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - Tests: - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] should return empty string when no operations". - "[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] should report stale story annotation" – writes file with @story non-existent.story.md, expects report string containing that path. - CLI report behavior: - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts – report command prints human-readable summary and exits 0; log output contains "Traceability Maintenance Report" and the stale file path. - Also tests invalid --format value causing exit code 2 with helpful error text.
- REQ-MAINT-SAFE (Safety, reversibility, not breaking functionality) - Safe defaults and error handling in detectStaleAnnotations: - Non-existent or non-dir roots yield [] (no throwing from library function); existsSync/ statSync errors in certain narrow tests are covered. - CLI safety behavior implemented in src/maintenance/cli.ts and src/maintenance/commands.ts: - runMaintenanceCli: - Prints help and returns EXIT_OK (0) when no subcommand or when -h/--help used. - Catches unexpected errors, logs `traceability-maint failed: ` and returns EXIT_USAGE (2). - For unknown subcommands, logs "Unknown command" and help text, then EXIT_USAGE (2). - handleDetect / handleVerify / handleReport / handleUpdate use structured exit codes (0, 1, 2) and do not throw to the top level. - Flags parsing (src/maintenance/flags.ts) validates --format, throwing clear Error on invalid values. CLI surfaces this as EXIT_USAGE + error text. - Tests (safety scenarios): - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update requires --from and --to and exits 2 when missing" – asserts code 2, error logged, help printed. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run does not modify files and exits 0". - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] report exits 2 and prints error on invalid --format value" – checks message includes "Invalid format: yaml" and expected options. - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect with non-existent --root exits 0 and reports no stale annotations" – verifies safe behavior for invalid root via CLI. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] prints help and exits 0 when no subcommand is provided" – ensures help is shown and no error is logged. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] detect catches filesystem permission errors and exits 2 with prefixed error message" – mocks fs.statSync to throw EACCES, expects traceability-maint failed: prefix and exit code 2.
4) Integration with plugin and ESLint ecosystem - src/index.ts: - Imports maintenance utilities: - detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport from "./maintenance". - Builds maintenance object and attaches it to the exported plugin: - const maintenance = { detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport }; - plugin.maintenance = maintenance; - Exported symbols: export { rules, configs, maintenance }; export default plugin; - Annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and @req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT. - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts confirms integration: - Imports from "../../src/maintenance" and asserts each maintenance tool is a function (detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport). - package.json bin configuration: - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } - Aligns with documented CLI usage in README and api-reference.
5) Documentation for maintenance tools - README.md (Maintenance CLI section): - Describes `traceability-maint` CLI purpose: maintain and audit @story annotations, focusing on stale references and safe batch updates. - Lists commands and semantics: detect, verify, report, update. - Provides usage examples: - npx traceability-maint --help - npx traceability-maint detect --root . - npx traceability-maint verify --root . - npx traceability-maint report --root . --format json - npx traceability-maint update --root . --from "stories/feature-authentication.story.md" --to "stories/feature-auth-v2.story.md". - user-docs/api-reference.md (Maintenance API and CLI section): - Documents programmatic API for: - detectStaleAnnotations(rootDir) - updateAnnotationReferences(rootDir, oldPath, newPath) - batchUpdateAnnotations(rootDir, mappings) - verifyAnnotations(rootDir) - generateMaintenanceReport(rootDir) - Includes parameters, return types, and behavior notes (e.g., story-only focus, no network, safe defaults). - Documents CLI commands detect/verify/report/update, CLI flags (--root, --json, --format, --from, --to, --dry-run), exit codes (0/1/2), and sample JSON payloads.
Overall, all REQ-MAINT-* requirements in the story are implemented, covered by passing tests, integrated into the plugin and CLI, and documented for users.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS are satisfied. Core functionality is present (detection, update, batch operations, verification, reporting) via the maintenance module and traceability-maint CLI. Quality and safety are addressed by conservative file operations, validation of inputs, safe defaults for non-existent roots, and structured exit codes. Integration is ensured by exporting maintenance utilities through the main plugin entry point and verifying exports in tests. User experience and error handling are validated by CLI tests that assert messages, JSON output, and behavior across success, dry-run, invalid flags, and filesystem error scenarios. Documentation in README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md clearly explains the maintenance tools, commands, and usage patterns. All associated tests pass, so this story is fully implemented.
